audience: People who have heard of Tau Net or hold AGRS and want to see what the testnet really does; then anyone curious about a blockchain with rules in logic.
question: What is a personal rule on Tau Net?
title: A wallet that says no: personal rules on Tau Net

scenes.say: On Tau Net a wallet can refuse its own owner. You write a rule for your own money, and from then on the chain holds you to it. Here are real ones, live.
scenes.caption: Rules people set

scenes.say: You do not have to write logic to make one. Say it in plain words, and the builder shows the same rule in the Tau language.
scenes.caption: Plain words to Tau

scenes.say: This wall holds every personal rule in force on the testnet. You can read each one, and take one for your own wallet.
scenes.caption: Every rule in force

scenes.say: One kind asks for a second signature on larger payments. It protects you from a mistake or a trick. It does not protect a stolen key: whoever holds the key can change the rule.
scenes.caption: A second signer

scenes.say: And here a rule does its work. The payment was signed with the right key, and the chain still said no, because the wallet's own rule forbids it.
scenes.caption: Right key, still no

scenes.say: The rules are written in the Tau language. The lessons are free, and each example is checked by the real engine. Next: run your own node.
scenes.caption: Free lessons

description: A personal rule is a rule a wallet gives itself, written in the Tau language and enforced by the chain: only these recipients, nothing above an amount, a second signature. This video shows real ones on the testnet and a payment being refused by one.

facts.o5: a user can give their own account a Tau rule that blocks some of their own transfers; the chain enforces it (tauhud.com/facts/, fact 'o5')
facts.approvals: a user can require a co-signature for their own large transfers (fact 'approvals')
